report.summary:
Repaired the start-owner basis retention so it holds the admitted invocation instead of the Public request; the owning HOW and the test were updated to match. All edits are in the three permitted files; no build, test or runtime was run.

1) run_invocation.ts: removed the early `yield* retainBasisLifetime(entryPrefix, call.invocation.invocationRef)` and its comment. The new hold `yield* retainBasisLifetime(admitted.successorPrefix, admission.invocationRef)` sits immediately after `const admission = admitted.admission`, before graph/basis construction. Why this is the fix: basis_admitted rows and the `RuntimeHistory.basisRowFact`/`retainBasisRowFact` lookup use the admitted invocation ref. Product computes that ref as a digest over a body that contains the Public ref (`publicRequestInvocationRef`), so the two always differ. Unchanged: the three continuation holds (now lines 1962, 2040, 2119), the resource acquireRelease, cleanup order (retention is released before the resource is abandoned) and all failure returns. Small extras: the helper's parameter is renamed `entryPrefix`→`coordinate`, and its doc comment now also describes the start.

2) Design doc §10.12, written before the code change: (a) the O1 lifetime paragraph now says the start holds `admission.invocationRef` on `admitted.successorPrefix`, separate from the Public request identity `call.invocation.invocationRef`/`publicRequestInvocationRef`, which no basis row carries. A start refused before admission holds nothing. Continuations and the scope lifetime are unchanged. (b) The Proof paragraph now covers the integrated check, physical close disposal (`closeAbgEventResource`) and the closed-coordinate case. It says explicitly that actual rollback disposal (`RuntimeHistory.truncate` after a failed append) is not driven and is unproved by this test.

3) t287-held-basis-lifetime.test.mjs: `run` now measures `observeExecutionBasisRowWork` immediately around only the actual `runInstalledDefinitionCallWithResource` call and returns that delta. Call construction and observer work fall outside the measurement. The first Run of the existing language-smoke fixture comes before every manual-handle probe. It asserts the call-only delta deepEquals {rowAdmissions:1, bodyDigests:1}. It then counts new basis rows (`owned().selection.select('kind:basis_admitted')`, admission ordinal greater than the cut before the call) and asserts exactly 1, plus zero retention after the call. The actual evidence goes into `observations.integrated` and into each failure message. The assertion is not loosened. The new comments say the count is specific to this fixture.

Checks performed: the three files matched their pinned starting bytes/sha256 before editing. Afterwards I rebuilt each file's starting version in memory (python3 -I reading its script from stdin, no files written) by reversing my exact replacements. All three matched their pins (run_invocation 109576/660f8cec…, design 201692/03c52118…, test 13528/79a37415…), so nothing changed outside my hunks. I verified the pinned Node at /opt/homebrew/Cellar/node/24.7.0/bin/node (86104016 bytes, fe1c0128…). Its `--check` on the edited .mjs exited 0, and the test was not executed.
